sections.h2: Where is Highland Park, Illinois, and what shapes the housing here?
sections.html:
Highland Park is a city in Lake County on the North Shore of the Chicago area, about 25 miles north of downtown Chicago. It covers 12.24 square miles of land and sits partly in Moraine Township and partly in West Deerfield Township, with ZIP codes 60035, 60036 and 60037.

Lake Michigan defines the layout. A bluff about 100 feet high runs along 6 miles of shoreline, and wooded ravines cut up to a mile inland. Elevations range from 580 to 725 feet above sea level. Houses near a ravine or the bluff edge are a different sale from a house on a flat street near a Metra stop, so a seller should expect buyers and cash purchasers to ask about the lot as much as the building.

The 2020 census counted 11,557 households and 12,405 housing units in the city, with 6.8 percent of units vacant. Highland Park had 30,767 estimated residents on July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: How did Highland Park grow, and why do so many older houses survive?
sections.html:
Two small lakefront settlements, St. John's and Port Clinton, came first. After the Chicago and Milwaukee Railroad built a depot, a plat was laid out in 1856. Highland Park was established as a city on March 11, 1869, and it annexed the village of Ravinia in 1899. St. Johns Avenue and Port Clinton Square still carry the old settlement names.

The housing stock reflects that early start. The National Register of Historic Places lists the Willits House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, along with homes by John S. Van Bergen, Howard Van Doren Shaw, Robert E. Seyfarth and David Adler. Landscape architect Jens Jensen lived in the city and designed projects that are on the register as well.

Owners of an architect-designed house usually have the original plans, permits and drawings in a drawer somewhere. Gather them before you talk to any buyer, because documented history is the one thing that can set a house apart from its neighbors.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning a home in Highland Park?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 show an owner-occupied housing rate of 83.8 percent, a median value of owner-occupied units of $607,300, and 11,787 households. Median gross rent is $1,925. About 87.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 24.3 percent of the population is 65 or older.

Those figures describe a city of long-time owners. Many sales here come from downsizing, estate settlement or a move out of the Chicago area, and each of those can leave a house to sell on a fixed timeline. The median household income is $168,094, and the mean commute to work is 27.5 minutes.

  • With most residents staying put year to year, a listing is often the first time a house has been priced in many years, so ask for recent sale records on your street.
  • Older construction means an inspection report can run long, and a buyer may ask for the original plans and permits.
  • Four Metra stations inside the city give buyers who work downtown a reason to pay attention to location.

sections.h2: Which schools and commuting routes matter to Highland Park buyers?
sections.html:
Public schools come from two districts. North Shore School District 112 operates an early childhood center, seven elementary schools and two middle schools. Township High School District 113 operates Highland Park High School and also Deerfield High School in nearby Deerfield.

US 41 is the main highway and connects Chicago to Milwaukee. Four Metra stations sit inside the city limits: Braeside, Ravinia Park, Ravinia and Highland Park. All are on the Union Pacific North Line, which starts in Chicago and ends in Kenosha, Wisconsin. Pace buses add local routes, O'Hare is about 20 miles southwest, and the Skokie Valley Trail runs through town.

Ravinia, the open-air pavilion that seats 3,200, has been the summer home of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra since 1936. Three public beaches, Rosewood, Moraine and Park Avenue, round out the lakefront. Mentioning stations, schools and the beaches in a listing is ordinary practice, and a cash buyer will weigh the same features when pricing.

sections.h2: What does the City of Highland Park require when a house sells?
sections.html:
The city taxes the transfer of real property under Chapter 97, Article X of its code. The city's declaration form prints the rate as $5.00 per $1,000 or fraction thereof of the full actual consideration, and states that absent a contract provision to the contrary, the transferor pays.

  • At least one seller and one buyer must sign the declaration.
  • A final water bill must be prepared and paid when the tax stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be scheduled up to five business days before closing.
  • The city wants a copy of the deed that will be filed with the Recorder of Deeds. Exempt transactions need the original deed.
  • Consideration includes the amount of the mortgage and the value of liabilities assumed.
  • Section 97.1004 lists exempt deeds, such as tax deeds, partition deeds, deeds where consideration is under $100, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.

Cards and personal checks are not accepted for the stamp. The Finance Department at 1707 St. Johns Avenue answers questions at 847.432.0800 or Finance@cityhpil.com.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Lake County, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Lake County deeds are recorded by the Recording Division of the County Clerk's Office, 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The Clerk's fee page lists $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and says the only extra charges at recording are the state and county transfer taxes that are due.

State law sets its own tax in 35 ILCS 200/31-10 at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration. When the transferring document says the property goes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of that calculation. Ask the title company or closing attorney for the county rate and the exact total, because they collect it at closing.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Highland Park house quickly?
sections.html:
A seller has three practical routes. Each trades price, certainty and effort differently.

  • List with an agent. The house goes in front of the widest group of buyers, and a bluff, ravine or architect-designed property may justify the wait.
  • Sell it yourself. You keep control of the contract, but you handle the showings, disclosures and negotiation.
  • Take a cash offer. Closing can move on the seller's schedule, and the house sells in its current condition, which suits an estate home, a rental with tenants or a place needing work.

Whichever route you choose, the city stamp, the final water bill and the deed filing apply to the sale. Start the water bill request early so closing does not stall on a missing meter reading.

If a cash buyer makes an offer, ask who pays each of the transfer charges listed above and get the answer in the contract. The city form says the transferor pays unless the contract says otherwise, so the contract is where that gets decided.

faqs.q: What is the population of Highland Park, IL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 30,767 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census count was 30,176.

faqs.q: Who pays the Highland Park transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the sales contract says otherwise. The city's declaration form states that, in the absence of a contrary provision, payment of the tax is the obligation of the transferor.

faqs.q: Do I need a final water bill to sell a house in Highland Park?
faqs.a: Yes. The city declaration form requires that a final water bill be prepared and paid at the time the transfer tax stamp is purchased, and a final meter reading can be scheduled up to five business days before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Highland Park house?
faqs.a: Highland Park is in Lake County, so the deed goes to the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office in Waukegan. Its fee page lists $70 for a standard document.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Highland Park?
faqs.a: North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools, and Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and Deerfield High School.
